newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - NOV 14.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - NOV 14.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:

- The opposition parties said that Elemer Kiss, State Secretary of the Prime Minister's office hindered the advancement of an investigation over irregular payments from the state privatisation agency to an advisor, Marta Tocsik.
- Mass transport in the capital may collapse next year, said mayors of Budapest districts.
- Trade unions proposed that the minimum wage for 1997 should be 18,300 forints.
- Csaba Lakatos, the man was shot at the Budapest race-course yesterday evening, will survive his injuries.
- The Finance Ministry said that honest tax-payers will win on the planned 1997 changes in the system of social security contributions.

- The opposition party Fidesz said the government will spark a serious conflict with the opposition if government representatives in the parliament do not support the nomination of Janos Bruhacs as member of the Constitution Court.
